messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] installation error
parts:
Hi Michael.

sorry for the delay; there were several issues that needed to be
solved a long the way.

First, the reason for this is that for the packages that I have that
are *not* on CRAN/Bioconductor there are no Mac binaries available,
and your settings are to install Mac binaries. I cannot build Mac
binaries, but someone else kindly help me to do this (for the ones
that are really necessary).

So, just retry to install again:

source("http://www.braju.com/R/hbLite.R")
hbInstall("aroma.affymetrix")

The hbInstall() function should be clever enough to detect you're
trying to install Mac binaries and then it will try to find a
workaround. The only Mac binary provided is R.native (downloaded as
*.tgz), and you'll be the first trying to install it. If you have a
problem with that one, we have to try something else. All other
packages, which are pure R package (no native code), should install
automatically from *source* (download *.tar.gz files).

Let us know if it works.

Alternatively, if you *do* have Apple Xcode Tools (version 2.4.1;
Apple's website), just do 'options(pkgType="source")' and redo the
above. That should work.

Cheers

/Henrik

might be others that experience the same or might now the reason. I
take the freedom to reply via the group mailing list; hope that is
ok.]

Hi,

I'll have a look at the installation script, but 'sfit' should not
install by default. When and how do you get this error? If it is
while running hbInstall(), could you please cut'n'paste the complete
output you get; that will help me track down why 'sfit' is being
installed (it shouldn't).

FYI, you will not need 'sfit' unless you are going to use the
AllelicCrosstalkCalibration class and that only applies to SNP chips.
So, if you're not doing that you 'source' approach should be fine.

Cheers

Henrik

Ok. If you're on OSX *Intel* it might be your lucky day, because I
think we've got a mac.binary install for Intel working (but not for
PPC). Try:

install.packages("sfit", contriburl="http://www.braju.com/R/repos/")
library(sfit)

If you don't get any error while loading the package that is a good
sign. Then retry AllelicCrosstalkCalibration.

/H
